growth_problem.classification_rule: no dominant pattern: none of the slowdown, collapse, volatility or growing rules fired
growth_problem.statement: The growth problem in Guatemala is mixed, with no dominant pattern: growth of 1.9 percent a year over the last decade is neither a slowdown against the 20-year record, nor a recent collapse, nor unusually volatile, nor fast by the rubric's rules. GDP per capita growth over 2016–2025 averaged 1.9 percent a year (2006–2025: 1.8; structural-peer median 1.5), 0.1 standard deviations above the convergence expectation and ranked 4 of 11 among structural peers. GDP per capita is at its peak to date (2025). A simplified single-break test finds a deceleration in 1979: average growth 3.0 percent before and 0.9 after. Investment (gross fixed capital formation to GDP) is 1.2 standard deviations below expectation given income at 16.3 percent of GDP; the private-public split is unavailable in prototype (IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset not ingested). Gross savings is at expectation given income; the current account balance is 3.6 percent of GDP and net FDI inflows are 1.5 percent of GDP. Structural change (G9) is not computed in the prototype. Exports to GDP is 0.9 standard deviations below expectation given income, and economic complexity is at expectation (the complexity gap). The relevant question is therefore: why is private investment low given income when the growth record shows no dominant pattern. Provisional top-split reading: credit boom without investment (real lending rate t = 0.9, real private credit growth 5.1 percent, investment t = -1.2).

top_split.label: credit boom without investment
top_split.reading: Conflicting: credit booming at high real rates without investment; check macro risk, crowding out and consumer credit

structural.rule: structural: 10 nearest by Euclidean distance in z-scores of log_gdppc_ppp, log_population, resource_rents (diagonal Mahalanobis), with a landlocked mismatch adding 1 to the squared distance (one sd of a continuous feature); micro-states below 300000 excluded; high-income economies excluded; fragile and conflict-affected economies excluded; candidates with an income observation before 2023 excluded

regional.rule: regional: same region (Latin America & Caribbean); income groups within 0 step(s) of Upper middle income until at least 6; capped at 15 nearest by log GDP per capita (PPP)

aspirational.rule: aspirational: GDP per capita (PPP) in 2000 within ±30% of the target's current 12670 and average growth since ≥ 3% a year; up to 10 by growth
